title: Anode and Graphite Q3 2026 Price Review
gist: Natural and synthetic anode active material (AAM) prices were flat from mid-June to mid-September 2026 because ~250ktpa of 2026 oversupply let buyers block pass-through of rising coke feedstock (+6.5% pre-calcined pet coke, +3.5% needle coke) and graphitisation tolling costs (+2.3%), squeezing producer margins. Coarse natural flake kept softening while fine mesh sat near all-time lows; Q4 watchpoints are whether the cost/price standoff breaks, Strait of Hormuz/Iran escalation, the November 2026 expiry of China's export-control suspension, and East African flake competitiveness.

insights.claim: Natural and synthetic anode active material prices held flat across all chemistries and capacities from mid-June to mid-September 2026, halting the natural-vs-synthetic price divergence that had widened earlier in the year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Midstream anode pricing has stalled; the natural/synthetic spread trade is no longer widening.
insights.locator: The divergence between natural and synthetic

insights.claim: AAM oversupply of nearly 250ktpa in 2026 gives downstream buyers enough leverage to stop anode producers from passing through higher coke feedstock costs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Structural oversupply caps anode pricing power; expect producer margins, not prices, to absorb input inflation.
insights.quote: AAM oversupply is set to be nearly 250ktpa in 2026
insights.locator: Why did anode prices stay flat

insights.claim: In Q3 2026 both natural and synthetic anode producers absorbed rising cost pressure into margins rather than raise prices and risk losing market share, because EV and ESS demand growth failed to notably outpace capacity additions.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Anode producer earnings face compression while feedstock rises; bearish margin read for graphite anode makers.
insights.quote: Producers absorbed the additional cost pressure rather than risk raising prices and losing market share.
insights.locator: “Q3 was characterised by a clear standoff

insights.claim: Q3 2026 contrasted with Q2 2026, when synthetic graphite producers were able to pass on price increases to buyers.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Pass-through ability is episodic; Q2 serves as the template for a possible delayed pass-through later.
insights.locator: Why did anode prices stay flat

insights.claim: Cell manufacturers were reluctant to raise anode bid prices partly because China introduced a 2% lithium battery consumption tax at the start of September 2026; existing orders were filled at current contract prices while new pricing agreements stayed under negotiation into October.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Chinese battery tax adds downstream cost pressure that pushes cell makers to resist upstream price hikes; watch October contract outcomes.

insights.claim: Low-sulphur pre-calcined pet coke DDP China rose 6.5% between June and August 2026, from RMB 4,200/tonne (USD 617.40) to RMB 4,475/tonne (USD 666.78).
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Synthetic graphite input costs are climbing again, pressuring synthetic anode producer margins.
insights.locator: What's driving synthetic graphite feedstock costs higher?

insights.claim: Pre-calcined pet needle coke, the higher-value feedstock for EV-grade synthetic anode material, rose a further 3.5% between June and August 2026, extending gains from earlier in the year.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: EV-grade synthetic anode faces the most persistent feedstock inflation; watch needle coke as the lead indicator for pass-through.
insights.locator: What's driving synthetic graphite feedstock costs higher?

insights.claim: Renewed Strait of Hormuz tensions from late June 2026 lifted Brent crude and Chinese slurry prices, which fed through the pet coke chain into higher synthetic graphite feedstock costs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Synthetic graphite costs are tied to oil geopolitics; Middle East risk is a direct input-cost driver for anodes.

insights.claim: Graphitisation tolling fees rose 2.3% between June and August 2026 on higher energy costs and growing pressure on tolling services, adding to synthetic anode producers' cost burden.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Energy-intensive graphitisation is a second cost layer beyond feedstock squeezing synthetic anode margins.
insights.locator: Higher energy costs and growing pressure

insights.claim: Natural graphite flake -100 mesh 94–95% C DDP China stayed flat at RMB 3,050/t in Q3 2026, extending a multi-month plateau close to an all-time low reached from Q4 2025.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Fine flake appears to have bottomed but shows no recovery; limited downside yet no catalyst for upside.
insights.locator: Why is natural graphite flake still under pressure?

insights.claim: Coarser natural graphite flake weakened in China between June and August 2026 on oversupply and lower-than-expected industrial demand: +100 mesh 94–95% C fell 1.9% and +80 mesh 94–95% C fell 0.9%, while +80 mesh FOB East Asia fell 4.2%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Coarse flake producers, especially those selling ex-China on FOB East Asia terms, continue to see price erosion.
insights.locator: Coarser material weakened modestly in China

insights.claim: If needle coke and pet coke keep climbing in Q4 2026, a delayed pass-through into synthetic anode active material prices is likely, echoing Q2 2026's pattern.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Watch for the cost/price standoff to break; synthetic AAM price increases could follow sustained coke inflation with a lag.
insights.quote: If needle and pet coke keep climbing, watch for a delayed pass-through into synthetic AAM prices, echoing Q2's pattern.
insights.locator: What is expected in Q4 for graphite and anode?

insights.claim: Further escalation of the Iran war and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz would extend feedstock cost pressure on synthetic graphite anode producers.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Middle East escalation is an upside risk to synthetic anode costs and a potential trigger for price pass-through.
insights.locator: Further escalation in the Iran war

insights.claim: China's temporary suspension of its expanded export controls to the US is set to expire in November 2026, a policy catalyst Benchmark flags for the anode and graphite market.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: November 2026 is a hard date for potential US supply disruption and ex-China graphite premiums.

insights.claim: East African flake graphite producers saw sharp price declines in Q3 2026, and if their competitiveness continues it would ease diversification of graphite supply chains away from China.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Cheaper East African flake supports ex-China sourcing strategies but pressures those producers' own margins.
